preRules.note: A noncharacter U+FDD0-U+FDDF in the text is not one of the tables' marks: U+FFFD, passed through and reported.
ଡ + nukta is ଡ଼ (normalised text keeps them apart: ଡ଼ is a composition exclusion); the composer writes the letter, DD.
ASCII " that opens a quote (at the start, after a space, a bracket or a dash) is “, two ‘ (22 22).
Any other ASCII " closes a quote: ”, two ’ (27 27).
ASCII ' that opens a quote is ‘ (22).
Any other ASCII ' (a closing quote, an apostrophe) is ’ (27).

The reph ର୍ (ra + virama starting a cluster) is written F6 after its syllable - the cluster and its vowel signs - and before ଂ ଁ ଃ (ର୍କା = 4C FF E6 F6; U+FDD0 marks it); on an independent vowel too, as the composer writes it (ର୍ଅ = 41 F6). Not after a virama: there ର belongs to the cluster (a ra-phala).

ୱ after a virama (the wa-phala, ସ୍ୱ) has no Shree spelling (the composer drops ୱ): it is written as ୍ବ, the ba-phala stroke B4, which is the glyph the composer writes for C + link + ବ and the shape Nirmala UI draws for both ୍ୱ and ୍ବ (r3\tbl-ori\round1\sheet2-00.png).

The ya-phala typed with ଯ (U+0B2F) is written as Shree's ya-phala ୍ୟ (U+0B5F, BF): Nirmala UI and Kalinga draw କ୍ଯ and କ୍ୟ alike (width 113.4 at 100 px, measured), and the composer's own C + link + ଯ answer is a visible virama and a full ଯ (FA BE).
The e-sign େ is written 7B before its cluster (U+FDD2 marks it; କ୍ରେ = 7B 4C FF F7).
ୈ = the e-sign before the cluster and the length mark ୖ F0 after it (କୈ = 7B 4C FF F0).
ୋ = the e-sign before the cluster and ା E6 after it (କୋ = 7B 4C FF E6).
ୌ = the e-sign before the cluster and the length mark ୗ F2 after it (କୌ = 7B 4C FF F2).

A letter + virama before କ୍ଷ keeps a visible virama, and କ୍ଷ is its ligature E4 (ଖ୍କ୍ଷ = 51 FA E4, କ୍କ୍ଷ = 4C FF FA E4, ଳ୍କ୍ଷ = C1 FF FA E4: the composer's spelling for every letter but ଙ, whose ଙ୍କ୍ଷ is a ligature of its own, 5F FF): U+FDD1 keeps ୍କ from being read as the subjoined କ.

postRules.note: U+FDD1 marks what draws nothing (a joiner) and keeps a pair's codes apart; it is not text.
